title: State that survives a reload
description:
Save a plugin's state to bytes before unloading it and restore it in the new version.

```
v1 state: score 120, level 3 -> 12 bytes
reload as v2 (adds "lives")
v2 state: score 120, level 3, lives 3 (default)
```
hints: Write the version first, then each field, as four bytes, lowest byte first: `for (int i{ 0 }; i < 4; ++i) bytes.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(value >> (8 * i)));`. Read a value back by shifting each byte into place and combining them with `|` (lesson 5.04's practice does the same). `std::memcpy` from `<cstring>`, already included, copies raw bytes in one call if you want to look it up.
Do not save pointers: after a reload the code and data they point at are gone.
requirements: The saved bytes start with a version number.
Version 2 reads version 1 data and gives new fields a default.
Unknown newer versions are refused, not guessed at.
stretch: Save a list of items with a count in front.
